viewer.name: campaigns
viewer.description: What goes out to the people who said yes, by action. Action audiences takes nothing more; read before any broadcast, it lists the audiences a broadcast may go to: everyone who said yes, every People list this workspace can count, and every list of the workspace's own (kept by hand, or by a rule), each with its kind and audience_id (the audience propose_campaign with action broadcast takes), its list token (the list people with action search takes), and four counts, because there are two consents and a yes needs a number to send to: can_be_sent_offers and can_be_sent_messages (who a promotional, or a utility or authentication, template reaches) and said_yes_to_offers and said_yes_to_messages (everyone who gave that yes, a number or not). partner.name: propose_lead_search
partner.description: Propose a search for businesses in the US the owner could reach, as a plan card they approve; nothing is searched or spent before that. The plan: what kind (who, plural, and who_one, one of them, with category_key as one lowercase word), how many (count: 50, 100, 200 or 500 unless they said a number), where (city with its two-letter region, a zip, or a region alone), the contact standard (contact: phone, or email checked), up to three terms (widest first), the criteria each with whether it is seen or likely and whether it is required, who to leave_out (chains, other kinds; short chips in plain words), looking_for (local_businesses, or people, online_sellers or other when that is what was asked: those are answered in words, not searched), and asked, the owner's words. seen is only for what a listing shows (a rating or review count, a website, an email, a phone that matches the site, open or closed) and is judged from those facts alone; what a business is or does (its kind, who owns it, what it serves or sells, who it treats) is likely, never seen, because a listing's name and category do not count as seeing it, and the kind of business itself is checked on every search without being written as a criterion. partner.name: propose_person
partner.description: Propose a change to someone in People, by action: a card the person asking approves, and nothing changes until they do. Action note takes contact_id, the id a read returned, body, the note in the words to keep (at most 600 characters), and for, who reads it: receptionist, for what should shape how the receptionist answers them (it reads the note before every answer to them), or team, for the team's own reminders and judgments (the receptionist never reads it). Call it when a customer gave their name or an email address in a message and their profile lacks it or says otherwise; read them first (people with action get), since an address a customer writes back when the receptionist asks for one is kept already, and never propose what the profile holds. partner.name: propose_reply
partner.description: Propose a reply to a customer, as a card the person approves before anything is sent. partner.name: propose_settings
partner.description: Propose a settings change the receptionist will follow, as one change object: add_closure (date, an optional until for a range, and an optional note), set_hours (one weekday's day with open and close, or both empty for closed), add_note (a title and the text the receptionist reads), or add_service (name, and an optional duration_min in minutes). Call it when they say they are closed, their hours change, the receptionist should know something, or they offer a new service; propose_autonomy is for what the receptionist may do alone. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask.

partner.name: propose_thread_verb
partner.description: Propose an Inbox action on a thread: take_over (a person answers from here), hand_back (the receptionist resumes), snooze (until an ISO time with its offset, or by default tomorrow at 10:00 by the business's clock), wake, archive, or resolve (close the open escalation; the thread stays). conversation_id is the id a read returned. Call it when they ask to take, hand back, snooze, wake, archive or resolve a thread; a reply is propose_reply with action draft, and how the receptionist treats the person is propose_person with action mode. It refuses in words when the action does not fit the thread's state: nothing to resolve, not snoozed, or nobody to hand back from.

partner.name: propose_whisper
partner.description: Propose a whisper: a sentence only the phone receptionist hears on a live call, worked into its next answer to the caller. call_id is a live call's id, from calls with action list and filter live, or from the Live page's row. Call it when they want to tell the receptionist something while the call is on; a call that has ended is refused in words, since there is nobody on the line. It shapes what the receptionist says next and never reaches the caller as written.

partner.name: report
partner.description: The Reports page for the last 7, 30 or 90 days: messages answered by the receptionist, by a person and left unanswered, the median and p90 reply time, calls and their minutes, new people, the escalation reasons, the change against the period before, a by-day series, the booking line (asked, then booked) where the calendar is read, and the Deals section where deals are on. Call it for how a period went or for a trend; the today tool has the day itself and its counts, and the Reports page on screen already holds this. days takes 7, 30 or 90 and nothing else. An empty period says so in empty; a range the report cannot answer is an error, said in words.

partner.name: today
partner.description: The Today page as it stands: who needs a person right now, the WhatsApp threads whose free-reply window is closing while the customer waits, today's calls, the standing of the receptionist, a recap and the day's counts. Start here for 'how are we doing', 'what needs me' or 'brief me', and read it for what Today holds when the person is on another page. partner.name: workspace
partner.description: The workspace, by action. Nothing changes because it was read.

owner.name: calendar
owner.description: The owner's calendar as the receptionist reads it. Action week takes day and an optional days and reads a day or a few: what is taken (in the calendar's own words, with the person in People when the title names one), whether the business is closed that day, and the windows the receptionist would offer; day is today, tomorrow, a weekday (mon..sun), a date (YYYY-MM-DD), or empty for the page's own week, and days is how many from there, at most 14. owner.name: calls
owner.description: Phone calls, as the Calls page and a call's page read them. Call action list to find calls by day, outcome or whether they are live, and a live call before proposing a whisper; a count of calls is the today tool's or the page's own, since the rows here are capped. Call action get when the transcript or the full summary is needed and the page on screen holds only the call's row. list returns at most 20 calls from the newest hundred; nothing changes because it was read. get caps the transcript at 40 turns, with transcript_turns saying how many there are; a call the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words.

owner.name: campaigns
owner.description: What goes out to the people who said yes, by action. Action audiences takes nothing more; read before any broadcast, it lists the audiences a broadcast may go to: everyone who said yes, every People list this workspace can count, and every list of the workspace's own (kept by hand, or by a rule), each with its kind and audience_id (the audience propose_campaign with action broadcast takes), its list token (the list people with action search takes), and four counts, because there are two consents and a yes needs a number to send to: can_be_sent_offers and can_be_sent_messages (who a promotional, or a utility or authentication, template reaches) and said_yes_to_offers and said_yes_to_messages (everyone who gave that yes, a number or not). Call action audiences before proposing a broadcast, and to say who a message would reach; call action playbooks to say what is running, and before proposing a playbook. Pick the template first, then quote its can_be_sent count as who the broadcast reaches, never a larger one; when that count is 0 and its said_yes is not, the ones who said yes have no number to send to: say so, and never send the owner to get a yes they already have. When a playbook's can_be_sent_now is 0 and said_yes_now is not, the ones who said yes have no number to send to, or heard from a broadcast this week: say so the same way. A list that cannot be counted here carries cannot_count and no counts; a null count means the page could not count it just now, and nothing has run because it was read.

owner.name: inbox
owner.description: The Inbox, on every wire (WhatsApp, text or email, whichever the customer last wrote on, named in channel). Action list takes filter and finds threads: needs_you (handed to a person), held (a draft waiting to send), waiting (taken over by a person), snoozed, or recent (all, newest first); each row has its state, its held draft when one waits, how long the customer has waited, whether the reply window is open, and its last three messages with who wrote them. Action thread takes conversation_id, the id a row here, the today tool or people returned, and an optional more, and reads one conversation: the person, its state, the open escalation, whether the reply window is open, the held draft with why it was held, and the messages with who wrote each and why the receptionist answered or held as it did. Action search takes words, what to look for, and an optional days, and finds them in what was said: every message of the workspace (what customers wrote; what the receptionist or the team wrote to them, sent or not; and a call's note in its thread) and every call's transcript, newest first, none older than days back from now (30 unless asked, at most 90). Call it for a word, the name of a thing or a phrase, such as did anyone mention parking this month; call action list for threads by their state, and action thread for one whole conversation, which a message hit's conversation_id opens (calls with action get opens a call hit's call_id). words are looked for as they were written or said, in English or Spanish, never stemmed, so park does not find parking: when nothing is found, try the other form; "a phrase in quotes" finds the words together, -word leaves out what holds it, or finds either side, and words that only leave things out find nothing. It returns at most 20 hits, with shown and more_available (whether there are more), each a message or a call with who it is with, when, the words around the match and the id that opens it; a message says its wire, who wrote it (customer, receptionist or you, as action thread says it, or call note for a call's note in its thread) and its status as action thread says it, and a message of the receptionist's or the team's whose status is queued (held, or not sent yet), canceled (before sending) or failed never reached the customer: say so, never that they were told it; a call says who placed it (called_by). A person's notes are not searched: people with action get reads them. Call action list to find threads by their state, and for what the page on screen does not hold; call action thread when the whole conversation is needed, since a row carries only the last three messages and the page on screen may hold only the thread's row. list returns at most 20 threads, with total_matching counted before the cap, so a count is the total and never the rows shown. thread returns the newest 30 messages, or 80 with more true; a conversation the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words.

owner.name: leads
owner.description: The lead finder, as the Leads page reads it, by action. Action searches takes nothing more and reads the workspace's lead searches, newest first, as the Leads page lists them: what was asked in the owner's words and when, its state or ending in words, how many qualified, need review and were counted, and, for a search that stopped to ask, its question; beside them, the rail's six counts of leads. Read it before proposing a search, so a plan is not repeated, and to answer about a search the person names. A search with a question is waiting for the owner's answer: words that answer it are propose_lead_search with amends set to that search's id, the same plan with the answer applied; to carry on unchanged or stop it, the owner presses Yes, keep going or Stop here on Leads. Action leads reads the businesses the searches found, as a view of the Leads page lists them: list is all (the default), ready, nurture (contacted), converted (talking), said_no or not_a_fit; search_id keeps one search's leads; class is qualified (the default: the counted ones), review (needs review) or excluded (left out), so a lead in review or left out is read only with its class; sort is fit (the default: strongest first), found (newest first), distance (nearest first), business (A to Z), rating (lowest first) or stage (ready first), and dir desc reverses it, so the best rated come first with sort rating and dir desc; words keeps the ones whose name, kind or area has them, as the page's box does. Each lead says its kind, area, class, fit or why it was left out, stage, email, rating, when it was found and its search; with the view's first page come the rail's six counts and, for an owner or a partner, this month's leads used and left. Call it for who the leads are or to find one in a class, and action lead for one lead's details. It returns at most 25 leads, matching counting the view's first five hundred of that class (words match within those) before the cap, and next_page, passed back as after, for the next five hundred. Action lead takes lead_id, the id action leads returned, and an optional search_id to read it as that search found it, and reads one lead as its peek on Leads shows it: its row, what its listing says about it, where it is and whether it is open today, its rating, why it fits, the checks made, where it was found, its phone, email and website. Call it when one lead's details are needed; a lead the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words. Action search takes search_id, the id action searches returned, and reads one search as Leads shows it at that search: its row as action searches says it, what the owner asked in their words and what the plan leaves out, how many emails were checked and how many leads have a phone, the qualified by fit (strong, look, long), and where to look next when it ran dry. Call it when one search is named or is the one on screen; a search the workspace does not hold, or one removed from Leads, is an error, said in words. Nothing here starts or changes because it was read, and every string is cut short.

owner.name: people
owner.description: People, the customers and callers, as the People page, a person's page and the Pipeline read them. Action search takes query and an optional list and finds people by name, WhatsApp name, address or three or more digits of a phone number, as the People page searches them; each row says their state in the pages' words, their last contact and last message, their conversation id, channels, consent, receptionist mode, how many calls, their next and last appointment when the calendar is connected, and their next step when they have one. Call it when the profile, the timeline or the notes are needed and the page on screen holds only their row; it returns their five newest conversations and calls, twenty timeline entries and twenty notes, and a person the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words. Action lists takes nothing more and reads every list People's rail shows: People's own lists this workspace can count, each with its token (the list action search takes), what it holds and how many are on it; the ones it cannot count here, with why; and the workspace's own lists, kept by hand or by a rule, each with its rule in the page's words and its count or why it cannot be counted, and the archived ones by name. Call it to say which lists there are and how many are on each, and action search with a list's token for who is on it. It counts over everyone in People, as a send counts them. Action pipeline takes nothing more and reads the Pipeline as its page builds it, where deals are on: the line over the table (the proposals out and what they come to, the ones waiting longer than usual, the lapsed, the clients and what they come to), the workspace's pace, and each group (consultations, proposals out, clients, passed or ended) with its count, what it comes to and its people, each with the deal's id, service and value, how long it has stood there, the page's chip and their next step. Call it for where deals stand, and action get for one person's deal in full. It returns at most 30 people across the groups, the groups' counts whole; where deals are off it says so, and People holds everyone.

owner.name: propose_autonomy
owner.description: Propose a change to what the receptionist may do alone: class (reply, booking, faq, reengage, campaign, reviews, or follow_up where deals are on) with mode (auto, veto, ask or never), or the reply confidence dial (min_confidence, 0 to 1, with mode empty). Call it when they want the receptionist to act on its own, wait for them, or hold its replies for a look; propose_person is for one person, and propose_settings for hours, closures, notes and services. veto is for replies only. Never for money: that class is locked by charter, so a request to change it is answered in words, not proposed. The modes as they stand are in this prompt above, so no read is needed first.

owner.name: propose_campaign
owner.description: Propose a campaign to the people who said yes, as a card the person approves: one message sent once, or a standing rule that sends on its own. Action broadcast takes template_id, one approved WhatsApp template, and proposes sending it to an audience, everyone who said yes or any list campaigns with action audiences names (audience_kind everyone; list for a People list, with its id as audience_id; saved for one of the workspace's own, with its audience_id), with params as the template's values in order (typed text, or @first_name, @business_name or @booking_link to fill per person), an optional scheduled_for as an ISO time with its offset (2026-09-20T15:00:00-04:00, never a bare date), and an optional name. Action playbook takes trigger and proposes a standing rule that sends one approved WhatsApp template to newly eligible people who said yes: trigger is quiet_30 (win-back), new_week (welcome), phoned_only (save our number), lapsed (no visit in 45 days), everyone_monthly (the month's offer), saved_list (on any list: its token from campaigns with action audiences in list, one of People's or one of the workspace's own, with policy_class campaign for an offer or reengage for a win-back), or, where deals are on, proposal_waiting (the proposal follow-up: one nudge per proposal waiting past the workspace's pace, one such playbook per workspace, its message carrying the proposal's link as @proposal_link); template_id is an approved template, or omitted for the trigger's starter when the workspace holds it; params are the template's values in order (typed text, or @first_name, @business_name, @booking_link, @proposal_link), filled in for a starter except a typed one such as the month's offer; run_hour is 9 to 20 by the business's clock (default 10) and cap_per_run defaults to 25. Call action broadcast for one message sent once, reading campaigns with action audiences first for the template ids, the audiences and their counts; call action playbook for a standing rule, reading campaigns with action playbooks first for what runs and who each moment reaches. When nobody can be sent a broadcast, say why: nobody said yes (point to their profiles) or the ones who did have no number to send to; never propose a broadcast to nobody. A broadcast's card includes nobody without a recorded yes and says how many it reaches; a playbook's card, once approved, runs under its class's autonomy mode, and a starter the workspace does not hold, or a typed value left blank, is refused in words.

owner.name: propose_deal
owner.description: Propose recording a deal on a person: stage proposed (a proposal went out, a new engagement), won (they said yes or paid, now a client), lost (they passed), or ended (the engagement ended). Optional: service, amount_cents with per (once, month or year: a proposal's value, or a client's agreed amount), a note, the proposal's web address (proposal_url), the last day it stands (valid_until, YYYY-MM-DD), with lost only why they passed (lost_reason: price, timing, elsewhere, no_reply, not_a_fit or other), and the next step on it, next_step (what, for the team) with next_step_due (YYYY-MM-DD, today or later), a note with a day the team sees on the deal. Call it when they say a proposal went out, someone became a client, passed or ended; a next step rides on that stage change, never alone, and a move names the open deal's service when there are two. It records what a person told you and never decides money; a move with no open deal to move is refused in words.

Call it for something about one person worth keeping on their page, such as a preference or what to remember next time; a fact about the business itself, such as parking or a policy, is a settings change and not a note, and a next step with a day is not a note: it rides on a deal's move (propose_deal), or is set on their page. Action details takes contact_id, the id a read returned, and name, email or both: the name the business calls them by and the address they can be written to, the two fields of their profile. Call it when a customer gave their name or an email address in a message and their profile lacks it or says otherwise; read them first (people with action get), since an address a customer writes back when the receptionist asks for one is kept already, and never propose what the profile holds. It never touches their notes, and the card shows each field as it was and as it becomes.

owner.name: propose_reply
owner.description: Propose a reply to a customer, as a card the person approves before anything is sent. Action draft takes conversation_id, the id a read returned, text, the reply itself, and voice, you for the person's own words or receptionist for the receptionist's voice, and proposes a new reply on a thread, on the wire the thread runs on. Action steer takes message_id, the held draft's id from inbox (with action list or thread), never a conversation id, and instruction, a rewrite in words ('shorter', 'mention Saturday is full', 'in Spanish') of a reply the receptionist is holding; the rewrite waits its turn like the first draft. Call action draft when they ask to reply, answer or write to someone, and action steer when they want a held draft changed. draft refuses a person who opted out and marks a closed reply window on the card; never quote or confirm a price in the text. steer refuses in words a reply that is no longer waiting, so read the thread first when in doubt.

owner.name: propose_settings
owner.description: Propose a settings change the receptionist will follow, as one change object: add_closure (date, an optional until for a range, and an optional note), set_hours (one weekday's day with open and close, or both empty for closed), add_note (a title and the text the receptionist reads), or add_service (name, and an optional duration_min in minutes). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, days mon..sun, times HH:MM. Call it when they say they are closed, their hours change, the receptionist should know something, or they offer a new service; propose_autonomy is for what the receptionist may do alone. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask.

owner.name: propose_team
owner.description: Propose a change to the team, by action; action invite, its one action today, takes email and role and proposes an invitation to the workspace by email, as operator (replies and handles threads; no settings or team) or viewer (reads everything, changes nothing). Call it when they want to add someone to the team; a role not offered here, such as owner, is answered in words. It becomes a card the person approves, and nothing is sent before that. Only an owner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that an owner can ask.

owner.name: propose_thread_verb
owner.description: Propose an Inbox action on a thread: take_over (a person answers from here), hand_back (the receptionist resumes), snooze (until an ISO time with its offset, or by default tomorrow at 10:00 by the business's clock), wake, archive, or resolve (close the open escalation; the thread stays). conversation_id is the id a read returned. Call it when they ask to take, hand back, snooze, wake, archive or resolve a thread; a reply is propose_reply with action draft, and how the receptionist treats the person is propose_person with action mode. It refuses in words when the action does not fit the thread's state: nothing to resolve, not snoozed, or nobody to hand back from.

owner.name: propose_whisper
owner.description: Propose a whisper: a sentence only the phone receptionist hears on a live call, worked into its next answer to the caller. call_id is a live call's id, from calls with action list and filter live, or from the Live page's row. Call it when they want to tell the receptionist something while the call is on; a call that has ended is refused in words, since there is nobody on the line. It shapes what the receptionist says next and never reaches the caller as written.

owner.name: report
owner.description: The Reports page for the last 7, 30 or 90 days: messages answered by the receptionist, by a person and left unanswered, the median and p90 reply time, calls and their minutes, new people, the escalation reasons, the change against the period before, a by-day series, the booking line (asked, then booked) where the calendar is read, and the Deals section where deals are on. Call it for how a period went or for a trend; the today tool has the day itself and its counts, and the Reports page on screen already holds this. days takes 7, 30 or 90 and nothing else. An empty period says so in empty; a range the report cannot answer is an error, said in words.

owner.name: today
owner.description: The Today page as it stands: who needs a person right now, the WhatsApp threads whose free-reply window is closing while the customer waits, today's calls, the standing of the receptionist, a recap and the day's counts. Start here for 'how are we doing', 'what needs me' or 'brief me', and read it for what Today holds when the person is on another page. It holds no drafts: inbox with action list and filter held has them, and inbox with action thread has a whole conversation. needs_you and calls are capped, the counts are not; nothing changes because it was read.

owner.name: workspace
owner.description: The workspace, by action. Action settings takes nothing more and reads the settings as the receptionist runs on them: the business and its time zone, hours, closures, services, languages, guardrails, notes, booking rules, when it escalates, whether the calendar and vision are on, the notifications (where alerts are emailed), the autonomy rows with their modes and limits (the reply policy's dials among them), and which channels are connected with their numbers. Call it for the reply policy's dials, the channels and the notifications; the hours, closures, services, notes, guardrails, booking notes and the autonomy modes are already in this prompt, so answer those from here without a read. A channels read that failed is said in could_not_read, never as no channels; propose_settings is what changes a setting. Action connections takes nothing more and reads what the workspace is connected to, in the Setup page's words: whether the receptionist answers and on which numbers; its phone line and whether the number its customers know is forwarded to it, WhatsApp, the email mailbox, the calendar and Google, each with its state and what the page says of it; and each domain it sends cold email from, with its state, what it has sent, its daily cap and what to do next. Call it for whether something is connected, or why not; action settings has the receptionist's own rules. Billing and the plan's price are not here: money stays out of Ask. Action notifications takes nothing more and reads this person's own notifications as the bell keeps them on the server: the last thirty days, sixty at most, newest first, each with its title, its first line, how long ago, whether it is unread for them and where it opens, and how many are unread; one they dismissed is gone. Call it for what the bell has told them. The bell also shows what the page works out in the tab (threads waiting on a person, missed calls, invitations), which this cannot read, so say the bell may hold more; billing's notices stay out of Ask. Action activity takes an optional person (a contact_id a read returned), kind (a verb or an event kind, exactly as the log spells it), day (YYYY-MM-DD, by the business's clock) and cursor (the next_cursor an earlier read returned), and reads who did what, as Settings › Activity lists it: both ledgers, newest first, each with when, who and what in the page's words, and where it opens; the usage, webhook and ingest records only when their kind is asked for. Call it for what a member or the receptionist did, and when. It returns the newest 30, with next_cursor for the ones after them while there are more; anything about money (billing, a partner's share) stays out of Ask. Nothing changes because it was read.
